Changelog

NeighbourNet 1.1.0

New features

  • visualise.network() gains interactive = TRUE, which returns an interactive network (a visNetwork htmlwidget) instead of a ggplot. It draws the same genes, edges, clusters and layout as the static plot, and adds:
    • hover tooltips with each gene’s layer, cluster, edge significance and the partners drawn, and each edge’s weight, significance and prior evidence;
    • click a gene, or pick it from the menu, to highlight its partners; filter by layer; zoom and pan;
    • distinct shapes per layer: g2 genes as diamonds filled with their cluster colour, g1 genes as circles, receptors as triangles and intermediate signalling steps as small labelled squares;
    • as in the static plot, dashed lines for co-expression only (undirected, not in prior knowledge), and solid lines with an arrow (activation) or a bar (inhibition) when prior knowledge supports the edge;
    • greyed-out genes for those with no edge above cutoff;
    • a legend below the network.
    It needs the visNetwork, htmlwidgets and htmltools packages, which are now suggested dependencies. The static plot (interactive = FALSE, the default) is unchanged.

Internal changes

  • visualise.network() is split into a computation step and a drawing step, so that the static and interactive plots share one computation.
  • First unit tests (testthat), covering visualise.network() on a small simulated data set.
